uncited: This family of methods addresses the problem of optimizing camera parameters (extrinsics and intrinsics) simultaneously with Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) weights, eliminating the reliance on pre-computed Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines like COLMAP [S2, unofficial].
By treating camera poses as learnable parameters, these methods enable 3D reconstruction from sparse or uncalibrated image sets [S2, unofficial].

What sets this family apart from siblings like [Time-dependent NeRF with Continuous Camera Motion](12399-time-dependent-nerf-with-continuous-camera-motion.md) is the explicit optimization of discrete camera poses per image rather than continuous motion functions, and from [Camera Preconditioning](12545-camera-preconditioning.md) by focusing on the joint gradient-based update of poses and scene geometry rather than preconditioning the optimizer for faster convergence.

All methods in this family share the core mechanism of differentiable rendering, where the rendered pixel color $\hat{C}(r)$ is a differentiable function of the camera pose $P$ and the NeRF parameters $\Theta$.
where $C(r)$ is the ground-truth pixel color.
The gradient $\nabla_P \mathcal{L}$ allows the camera pose to be updated via an optimizer (e.g., Adam, SGD) in lockstep with the NeRF weights.
**Ray Casting:** Computing ray origins $\hat{o}$ and directions $\hat{d}$ from pixel coordinates using current camera estimates.
**Differentiable Rendering:** The volume rendering integral is computed via discrete summation, allowing backpropagation through the ray marching process to the pose parameters [S2, unofficial].
**Joint Optimization:** Separate optimizers or a combined optimizer are used to update NeRF weights and pose parameters, often with different learning rates to stabilize convergence [S2, unofficial].
The problem of joint pose and NeRF optimization emerged as a solution to the dependency on accurate Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines, which can fail on textureless or repetitive surfaces.
